blocks.heading: A coherent marketing plan
blocks.text: A marketing plan sets a target, objective and coordinated product, price, promotion and distribution decisions, with resources, actions and review. The elements should reinforce the same need: a premium fragile product, bargain price, mass discount message and unreliable handling would conflict. Specify enough to act and monitor results, while treating sales expectations as assumptions to test. Marketing planning sits inside the broader business plan and must fit capacity and finance.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Tula Tools can make a small reliable range of durable tool bags for local tradespeople. Full unit cost is N$80 and research supports testing a price of N$120. The owner has limited promotion funds and can supply by workshop collection. Model plan: target local tradespeople needing durable organised storage; objective—test paid demand and repeat interest over four weeks within current capacity. Product—durable tool bag with practical compartments and clear care information. Price—test N$120 against N$80 stated unit cost, review actual uptake and costs. Promotion—local demonstration and a concise accessible notice explaining the benefit and collection arrangements. Distribution—direct workshop collection, recording orders to avoid exceeding capacity. Action/review—owner confirms material supply, schedules a small trial, records paid units and feedback weekly and revises the offer before expansion. This is a connected plan, not four unrelated definitions.
